key_insight: A new large-deviation framework for local weak wave turbulence predicts both typical spectrum fluctuations and rare events, while revealing long-range correlations driven by bulk fluxes and boundary forcing.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to quantify finite-size, intermittent, and non-equilibrium effects in wave systems, improving prediction of spectra beyond mean kinetic theory.
method: Derive a large deviation principle specialized to local wave interactions.
Analyze Gaussian fluctuations around out-of-equilibrium spectra.
Decompose two-point correlations into bulk-flux and forcing-driven contributions under fixed-flux boundary conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations and first-time computation of correlation contributions using a boundary-condition-adapted method, but does not mention experimental or simulation data.
watch_item: The framework is tailored to idealized local weak turbulence and may need careful adaptation when interactions are nonlocal, strongly nonlinear, or the forcing/boundary conditions are not well controlled.
paper_title: Dynamical large deviations and long-range correlations for local weak wave turbulence
